title: Chip Designing  ·  OpenROAD
subtitle: RTL to GDSII, one calm step at a time

steps.title: Write your RTL
intro: Describe your hardware in Verilog. Your editor opens with a small skeleton.
tips: The top module is already named {name}. Keep that name.
Keep a clock input called clk, because the constraints file refers to it.
Save with Ctrl+S. I will notice the save, then press Enter here to continue.
stub: // The top module must be called @NAME@ and have a clock input named clk.
// add more ports here, for example:  , input wire [7:0] a

steps.title: Write your testbench
intro: The testbench drives your design and checks the outputs, so you know it works before it becomes silicon.
tips: Instantiate your design as dut, drive the inputs, compare the outputs, count errors.
Print PASS when everything matches. I will run the simulation and show you the result.

steps.title: Constraints (constraint.sdc)
intro: Constraints tell the tools how fast your chip has to run.
tips: clk_period is the clock period in ns. Smaller means faster and harder.
Input and output delays are set to 20% of the period.
A ready-made file is in place. Most designs only change clk_period.

steps.title: Flow settings (config.mk)
intro: config.mk names the design, the platform and the die size.
tips: Only the die size ever needs changing. Tiny designs: keep DIE_AREA and CORE_AREA.
Bigger designs, such as a CPU: comment out those two lines and enable CORE_UTILIZATION.
A cramped die is the usual cause of routing trouble.

steps.title: Synthesis
views: Netlist as read into the database
about: Yosys turns your RTL into real logic gates from the platform's cell library.

steps.title: Floorplan
views: Rows and tap cells, before the power grid
about: Chooses the die and core area, lays out the rows where cells sit, places the IO pins and builds the power grid.

steps.title: Placement
about: Puts every gate at a legal spot on the rows, keeping connected cells close together.

steps.title: Clock tree
views: Clock buffers inserted (Windows > Clock Tree Viewer)
about: Builds a balanced tree of buffers so the clock reaches every flip-flop at almost the same moment. A design with a single flip-flop skips this.

steps.title: Routing
steps.hint: A cramped die is the usual cause. Enlarge DIE_AREA in config.mk and rebuild.
about: Draws the real metal wires between cells and fixes design-rule violations. This is the longest step.

steps.title: GDSII
about: Adds filler cells and writes the final GDSII layout file, the file a foundry would receive.
